proven themselves to be valuable building blocks in propargyla-
tion, allenylation,<sup>[3-4]</sup> and many other useful transformations.<sup>[5]</sup>

readily available starting materials. Currently, the two major ap-

Results and Discussion
Our investigation commenced with the addition of alkynyl
Grignard reagent 2a to an α-halogenated gem-diboron compound
1 (Table 1). According to our previous studies,<sup>[17]</sup> the halogen
substituent and the cosolvent were found crucial to the reaction.
After initial tests, excellent yield was observed when the
gem-diboryl iodide 1c was employed as the substrate (entries
1—3). Due to the lower reactivity of the sp-hybridized carbanion,
magnesium-iodine exchange, which was previously observed with
aryl and alkyl Grignard reagents, did not occur. To our delight, the
propargyl gem-diboron product 3a was not generated, which is
otherwise challenging to separate. The addition of toluene as the
cosolvent was not necessary compared to pure THF or diethyl
ether/THF system (entries 4 and 5). However, with toluene, the
reaction was homogeneous, which was preferred for further
study. 1,4-Dioxane, DME, and cyclohexane, however, hampered
the reaction efficiency and provided 3a as the major product
(entries 6—8). Lastly, alkynyl lithium and zinc reagents were
investigated, and the desired product was also observed, albeit in
lower yield (entries 9 and 10).

Conclusions
In summary, we have disclosed the first example of accessing
1,3-diboryl allenes from gem-iododiboron compounds in the
presence of alkynyl Grignard reagents. The reaction is highly effi-
cient and can accommodate steric hindrance and various func-
tional groups. Mechanistic studies have suggested that the cas-
cade process consists of a formal substitution and a subsequent
isomerization. The isotope-labeling crossover experiment indi-
cated that the isomerization proceeds through an unconventional
intermolecular boryl group transfer. Utilization of the products
was also briefly demonstrated.
Experimental
In an argon-filled glove box, to a 15 mL vial equipped with a
magnetic stir bar was added the iododiboron compound (0.1
mmol, 1.0 equiv.). The vial was sealed with a polypropylene
open-top cap with PTFE/silicone septum, then removed from the
glove box. Toluene (1.0 mL) was added and the vial was cooled in
an ice-cold water bath. Grignard reagent (0.11 mmol, 1.1 equiv.)
was slowly added. The mixture was then warmed to room tem-
perature and stirred for 3 h. Upon completion, the reaction was
quenched with sat.

Conclusions
In summary, we have disclosed the first example of accessing
1,3-diboryl allenes from gem-iododiboron compounds in the
presence of alkynyl Grignard reagents. The reaction is highly effi-
cient and can accommodate steric hindrance and various func-
tional groups. Mechanistic studies have suggested that the cas-
cade process consists of a formal substitution and a subsequent
isomerization. The isotope-labeling crossover experiment indi-
cated that the isomerization proceeds through an unconventional
intermolecular boryl group transfer. Utilization of the products
was also briefly demonstrated.
Experimental
In an argon-filled glove box, to a 15 mL vial equipped with a
magnetic stir bar was added the iododiboron compound (0.1
mmol, 1.0 equiv.). The vial was sealed with a polypropylene
open-top cap with PTFE/silicone septum, then removed from the
glove box. Toluene (1.0 mL) was added and the vial was cooled in
an ice-cold water bath. Grignard reagent (0.11 mmol, 1.1 equiv.)
was slowly added. The mixture was then warmed to room tem-
perature and stirred for 3 h. Upon completion, the reaction was
quenched with sat.
